speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan
text: asked the Minister for Transport (a) how will the new on-board unit (OBU) for vehicles under the next generation Electronic Road Pricing system be effective in regulating traffic congestion on the roads if motorists are unaware of the exact costs of using certain roads; and (b) whether the payment options using the OBU will be aligned to the car park payment options for all car parks in Singapore.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng
text: asked the Minister for Transport (a) what is the comparative cost per unit of the In-Vehicle Unit of the current ERP system relative to the on-board unit of ERP 2.0; (b) what is the anticipated lifespan of the ERP 2.0 system before it becomes obsolete; and (c) whether LTA has assessed if the crucial functions of ERP 2.0 system can be replicated to a smartphone App to offer motorists a choice between exclusively utilising the App and installing the On-Boarding Unit.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: The current Electronic Road Pricing (ERP) system has served us well for 25 years, since 1998, in mitigating traffic congestion and keeping traffic smooth along key roads.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: However, it is reaching the end of its operational lifespan.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Obsolete parts in the gantries as well as the existing in-vehicle unit (IU) would require customised production or the use of less reliable substitutes which could affect the effectiveness and reliability of the system.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Running such an ageing system will not be cost effective.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: The new system allows LTA to be more agile in managing congestion.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: LTA will have valuable insights into our traffic conditions to make quicker interventions without the need to build costly physical gantries in land-scarce Singapore.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: ERP 2.0 is planned with long-term use in mind.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: The system architecture is based on open standards and a modular design, which will allow for future upgrades, that will help keep ERP 2.0 relevant and up-to-date.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Mr Lim Biow Chuan asked how motorists would be aware of ERP charges with the new on-board unit (OBU).

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Under ERP 1.0, the charge is displayed on the IU when the vehicle crosses the gantry.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: During the transition from ERP 1.0 to ERP 2.0, when the new OBUs are being progressively installed, there will be no change to how motorists will be charged as charging will continue to be carried out by the gantries.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: When the transition to ERP 2.0 is completed, charging will be carried out through GNSS as the physical gantries are progressively decommissioned.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: There will be signages which demarcate the points at which ERP will be charged and the OBU will provide an alert when the vehicle approaches an ERP-charging location and indicate the relevant charges.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: For motorists who choose not to install the OBU screen, this information will be made available through compatible mobile applications on smartphones.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Information on ERP charged locations and ERP rates will also be announced and made available publicly on the OneMotoring website, which is similar to the current practice.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Mr Lim Biow Chuan also asked whether the OBU will be aligned to the car park payment options.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: The OBU is designed to work with existing systems, including ERP and Electronic Parking System carparks.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Motorists can continue to pay via valid Contactless e-Purse Application (CEPAS) cards such as EZ-Link Motoring Card, NETS Flashpay and NETS Motoring Card, but not cash cards, as these are being phased out.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Mr Yip Hon Weng asked on the comparative costs between the IU and OBU.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: For all eligible existing Singapore-registered vehicles, the OBU will be installed free of charge if completed within the two-month period stated in LTA's notification.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: It will also come with a five-year warranty.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: All new vehicles purchased from first quarter of next year will be fitted with the new OBUs.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: The costs of the new OBU are being finalised and will be announced in due course.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Mr Louis Chua asked when does the Government intend to commence the implementation of distance-based charging.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Distance-based charging is a different approach for congestion management and any plans to implement it must take many factors into consideration.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Ms He Ting Ru asked whether our considerations on data usage had been updated.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Our reply to her on this issue in 2020 remains valid.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: To reiterate, there are strict safeguards in place to govern the collection, usage and storage of data.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: For instance, LTA will only use anonymised or aggregated data for traffic management and transport planning purposes.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: For vehicle-specific data, LTA will only use it for payment, charges and enforcement, such as against non-payment of ERP charges.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: LTA also adheres to Government-wide standards for data security, including strict guidelines on data sharing with other Government agencies.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Robust safeguards are in place to prevent unauthorised access.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: There are also criminal penalties for unauthorised disclosure and improper use of information.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: The Ministry of Home Affairs is replying to a separate Parliamentary Question on the use of ERP 2.0 data by the Singapore Police Force and intelligence agencies.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Mr Yip Hon Weng also asked if LTA had access if the ERP 2.0 system could be wholly replaced using a smartphone.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: First, to identify the vehicle's location and communicate with the ERP system.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Second, to process transactions in real time safely and securely.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Third, to notify motorists on the ERP charge and other key traffic information.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: For the first function, the precision of smartphone location data can vary across different devices and increases the risk of erroneous charging.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: As a common and trusted standard issue device for all Singapore-registered vehicles, the OBU can better ensure reliability and performance and reduce significant downstream operational challenges, such as disputes regarding charging inaccuracies.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: It is also crucial to ensure that there are strict safeguards for data collection and storage.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: The OBU has been designed with robust security measures and tested extensively to ensure that it can handle real-time charging transactions and data securely.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Data stored in the OBU cannot be directly accessed by motorists or external mobile applications and are designed to be tamper-proof, with a high level of security and encryption.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Therefore, while the OBU can broadcast data, it is not designed to receive data or instructions from an external mobile application.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: For the second function, to allow the smartphone to process the ERP transactions, motorists will have to start their mobile apps, key in their passcode or use biometric authentication to enable ERP charging each and every time they travel.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: This is inconvenient to motorists and some may inevitably forget to start their mobile apps for the ERP.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: [Pursuant to Standing Order No 22(3), provided that Members had not asked for questions standing in their names to be postponed to a later Sitting day or withdrawn, written answers to questions not reached by the end of Question Time are reproduced in the Appendix.]
